question.text: A COVERED call (long stock + short call) generates income from premium but:

explanation.text: The Logic: A covered call combines a long position in the underlying stock with a short call option on that same stock. The premium received from writing the call augments income but, because the call gives the buyer the right to acquire the stock at the strike, any appreciation in the underlying above the strike accrues to the call-buyer rather than the writer. The writer's upside is therefore capped at the strike price plus the premium received, while the downside remains substantially similar to that of an unhedged long stock position (offset only by the premium received). The Trap: "Unlimited loss" describes a naked short call or a short stock position, not a covered call. "Unlimited gain" ignores the assignment risk above the strike. "No effect" contradicts the basic mechanics of writing a call against owned shares. Only "limited upside (capped at strike)" describes the defining payoff feature of a covered call. Note: The cited pages of the NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook (p.100-p.101, p.321-p.322) define call options and discuss protective puts and futures hedging but do not explicitly cover the covered-call strategy or the capping of upside from long stock plus short call in the pages checked. The framing above is general options-strategy knowledge.
